headings: Getting your ballot pack by email
How to complete your postal vote
How to do your postal vote
https://www.vec.vic.gov.au/voting/2026-s.text: Vote by post | Victorian Electoral Commission Please enable JavaScript in order to get the best experience when using this site. Jump to main navigation Jump to main navigation Jump to main content Toggle navigation Victorian Electoral Commission Victorian Electoral Commission logo Languages Toggle search Search Type a minimum of three characters then press UP or DOWN on the keyboard to navigate the autocompleted search results Search button Close search bar Back to 2026 state election Home Voting 2026 state election Vote by post On this page Vote by post Listen On Saturday 28 November, Victorians will vote to elect the next Victorian Parliament. Apply to vote by post in the 2026 state election from now until 6 pm on Wednesday 25 November. Apply early to allow enough time for the ballot pack to reach you. Apply online The quickest way to apply for a postal vote is by using our online form. Apply for a postal vote (within Victoria) Apply for a postal vote (outside Victoria) Having technical issues with the application form? Verification question When you apply for a postal vote online, you must choose a verification question and nominate an answer. Keep a record of your answer. You must include it on the declaration on your ballot pack when you return your ballot papers. If you asked for emailed ballot papers, you'll need your answer to download your ballot pack. We use this question to confirm your identity and admit your vote to the count. Overseas voters If you’re overseas, we recommend you get your ballot pack by email. You can select this option when you apply using the online form. If you receive your ballot pack by email, you will need to post it back or drop it off at one of our international venues. You cannot send it back to us by email. Apply using a paper form If you prefer, you can also complete a paper application form to vote by post. Paper application forms are available from: Australia Post offices in Victoria VEC head office – Level 11, 530 Collins St, Melbourne your district election office. Election office details will be available from 9 am on Wednesday 4 November. Who sends postal votes Postal vote applications must only be sent by us or through Australia Post outlets. Candidates or political parties, or anyone else, are not allowed to send you postal vote applications. If you receive a postal vote application from anyone other than us: don't fill it out report it to us as a breach of the Electoral Act 2002. Getting your ballot pack by email If you’re outside Victoria, or your mail service is slow or unreliable, we can email you a ballot pack. We'll send you a link to download and print your ballot pack. You’ll need access to a printer. If you receive your ballot pack by email it does not mean you can vote online. There is no online voting in this election. headings: State election 2026: When and where to vote

Jump to main navigation Jump to main navigation Jump to main content Toggle navigation Victorian Electoral Commission Victorian Electoral Commission logo Languages Toggle search Search Type a minimum of three characters then press UP or DOWN on the keyboard to navigate the autocompleted search results Search button Close search bar Back to 2026 state election Home Voting 2026 state election Voting options On this page Voting options Listen There are many ways you can vote in the 2026 state election. We also have information about accessible voting options this election and what to do if you're away from Victoria. Vote early Skip the queues and vote early between Wednesday 18 and Friday 27 November. Early voting is open 9 am to 6 pm daily except Sunday 22 November. You don’t need a reason to vote early. Find early voting centres using our election venue locator. Find early voting centres All early voting centres will have: an assistive hearing device at least one voting screen at wheelchair height or a table-top voting screen magnifying sheets maxi pencils information about how to vote in other languages. Vote on election day Find election day voting centres All election day voting centres will have: at least one voting screen at wheelchair height or a table-top voting screen magnifying sheets maxi pencils information about how to vote in other languages. Find out what happens at a voting centre Low-sensory voting We offer low-sensory voting for people who need a quieter voting experience. Low-sensory voting sites will be open on Tuesday 17 November from 10 am to 4 pm. There will be one low-sensory voting site in each district. Low-sensory voting is for people who: are neurodivergent have sensory needs. are carers, support workers and anyone supporting people who are neurodivergent or have sensory needs. While voting you will notice: extra space around voting booths a quieter venue lower or natural lighting where possible staff who can support voters with non-visible disabilities. Learn more about low sensory voting Braille ballot papers We can post you a braille ballot paper if you're blind or vision impaired. Registrations for braille ballot papers have now closed. You don’t need to do anything if you’ve already registered – you only need to register once. If you have registered, we'll post ballot packs after nominations have closed and we’ve confirmed all the candidates. If you missed out on registering, you might be eligible to vote by phone from Wednesday 18 November.
